findings.problem: A render delay of one slot or more silently corrupts the slot grid in --mode vsync. Nothing bounds --render-delay-ms (line 141 only checks >= 0). When the tick blocks past the next vsync (line 429), the next CADisplayLink tick fires as soon as the run loop is free, with targetTimestamp about 8.33 ms after that fire time, so it is not on the vsync grid. Every target difference is then about delay + work, the median fit at lines 448-454 takes that as S, and line 456 advances the slot index by 1 per tick instead of round(gap / 8.33 ms). The report then prints a wrong link rate and a Pacer result for a grid that does not exist. No deadlock and no unbounded pile-up occurred.
findings.evidence: Ran: probes/present_probe --seconds 6 --link-hz 120 --source counter --display-mode keep --window small --mode vsync --present plain --render-delay-ms 20. Exit 0, callbacks=270. Report: "link rate: requested 120.0 Hz, measured 44.833 Hz (1 / S median); step = 1 slot(s) per position; S median = 22.3052 ms"; gapCallbacks=0; pacer corrections=100 collision=38 pushedLate=60; "lead (targetTimestamp - tick entry) p50=8.325". CSV target_time differences: 23.646 22.098 24.255 23.428 20.978 22.454 ... 14.280 29.882 ms, none a multiple of 8.333 ms; slot column advances 0,1,2,3.
findings.fix: Next to line 141: die when vsyncMode and renderDelayMs >= 1000 / linkHz (leave margin for encode, e.g. slot minus 1.5 ms). Optionally also flag the run in the report when 1 / sMedian differs from --link-hz by more than 1 %.

findings.problem: The G1 report does not count a run of shown rows whose presented_time is 0. The loop at lines 811-815 only measures intervals between rows with a non-zero presented time, so N consecutive zero rows count as one out-of-band interval, and as none when the run is at the end of the capture. The latency filter at line 791 drops the same rows. The G1 RESULT line (832) then reports in_band_pct and max_glitches_per_15s for only the measured part of the run. This logic predates the change, but --mode vsync --present at-slot is the first case that hit it, and row 2 of the implementer's table rests on it.
findings.evidence: Implementer's own at-slot / delay 0 run: shown=1199, presented_time == 0: 753, content intervals count=325, last out-of-band at 7.40 s of a 20 s run, yet "G1 RESULT: latency_p99_ms=24.96 in_band_pct=98.462 max_glitches_per_15s=5". My repeat of the same command had 3 zero rows of 1199 and gave in_band_pct=93.116, max_glitches_per_15s=70, latency p99=33.27 ms.
findings.fix: In counterReport, count every shown row after warm-up with presented == 0 as an out-of-band event (add its callback time to outT), or print measured/shown in the G1 RESULT line and print n/a for in_band_pct when the zero rows exceed a small share. Re-run the at-slot row before using it.

findings.problem: renderDelayTicks is computed at line 77, before the validation at line 141. A non-numeric value (parsed as -1), a negative value, nan or a huge value makes UInt64(Double) trap, so the intended "FATAL: --render-delay-ms must be a number >= 0" is never printed. It also kills --pacer-selftest when the flag is present.
findings.evidence: probes/present_probe --render-delay-ms abc --mode vsync --source counter: exit 133 (SIGTRAP), no FATAL line. Same for -1, nan, 1e30, and for --pacer-selftest --render-delay-ms -2.
findings.fix: Move the renderDelayTicks computation below the line 141 check (and make that check reject non-finite values and values >= one slot, see first finding).

findings.problem: In --mode vsync the flags --min-duration and --at-time are silently ignored (line 586 takes the vsync branch first, line 144 does not reject them), but the config: line (860) still prints them as if applied.
findings.evidence: probes/present_probe --seconds 4 --link-hz 120 --source counter --display-mode keep --window small --mode vsync --runloop main --min-duration 0.0167 --at-time 1 printed "config: mode=vsync present=plain ... min-duration=0.0167 ... at-time=true" and ran a plain present.
findings.fix: At line 144 add: die when vsyncMode and (minDuration > 0 or atTime).

findings.problem: Exit race, --mode vsync with --runloop thread only. finish() invalidates the CADisplayLink from the main thread, sleeps 0.3 s, then reads cbTime, lead, cpu, pacer and rows. In link mode a callback never blocks, so 0.3 s is enough. In vsync mode a tick already in flight can stay inside mach_wait_until (line 429) or nextDrawable() (line 484, up to the 1 s timeout) for longer than 0.3 s and then run counterCallback and render() (unlocked cbTime.append at 435, rows writes at 478-491, cpu.append at 590) while the main thread is building the report.
findings.evidence: By reading only. Concrete trigger: --render-delay-ms 400 (accepted today), tick entered less than 100 ms before the --seconds timer fires. Not run.
findings.fix: The delay bound from the first finding removes the mach_wait_until case. For the nextDrawable() case, set an atomic stop flag in finish() and return at the top of vsyncTick and after nextDrawable() when it is set, or sleep past the 1 s drawable timeout in vsync mode.

findings.problem: The G1 RESULT line hides a trailing block of shown rows whose presented_time is 0. Such rows are dropped from `pres`/`lat` at line 774, and line 811 only forms intervals between two consecutive non-zero rows, so zero rows that are never followed by a non-zero row produce no out-of-band interval and no latency sample. The comment at lines 807-808 says this case "is not hidden"; that holds only when a later non-zero row exists. State: `--mode vsync --present at-slot`, 753 of 1199 shown rows with presented_time 0, all after about 7.4 s. Wrong result: `in_band_pct=98.462 max_glitches_per_15s=5 latency_p99_ms=24.96` for a run where no present was confirmed on glass for the last ~12.6 s of 20 s.
findings.evidence: Implementer's own run file $TMPDIR/run_presentatslot.txt: `content intervals ... count=325 ... out of band: 5`, last out-of-band entry `8.33ms@7.40s`, `shown rows with presented_time == 0: 753`, `G1 RESULT: latency_p99_ms=24.96 in_band_pct=98.462 max_glitches_per_15s=5 mode=vsync present=at-slot render_delay_ms=0`. 325 intervals x 16.68 ms = 5.4 s, so the measured rows end at about 7.4 s and the remaining 753 rows (12.6 s) are all zero. The interval logic predates this change, but the new mode is where it produced a passing-looking gate line. My two at-slot delay-0 runs had only 2 and 3 zero rows, so the 753 event itself did not reproduce.
findings.fix: Count every shown row with presented_time == 0 after the warm-up as an out-of-band event (add its callback_time to `outT`), or at minimum append `zero_presented=<n>` to the G1 RESULT line and print n/a for in_band_pct when the last non-zero presented row is more than one position before the last shown row. Correct the comment at 807-808.

findings.problem: `renderDelayTicks = UInt64(renderDelayMs / 1000 * 1e9 * ...)` runs at line 77, before the validation at line 141, and `UInt64(Double)` traps on negative, NaN and out-of-range values. Input: `--render-delay-ms abc`, `-1`, `nan` or `1e30`. Result: the process dies with SIGTRAP (exit 133) and prints nothing; the intended `FATAL: --render-delay-ms must be a number >= 0` at line 141 is unreachable for these inputs. It also kills `--pacer-selftest --render-delay-ms -1`, because line 77 is above line 135. `nan` would pass the `< 0` check at 141 in any case.
findings.evidence: Scratch binary: `present_probe_review --render-delay-ms abc --mode vsync --source counter --seconds 1` -> exit=133, empty output; same for -1, 1e30, nan; `--pacer-selftest --render-delay-ms -1` -> exit=133.
findings.fix: Move the `renderDelayTicks` computation below the validation block, and change the check at line 141 to `if !(renderDelayMs >= 0 && renderDelayMs < 1000) { die(...) }` so NaN and huge values are rejected too.

findings.problem: In `--mode vsync` the present branch at line 586 ignores `--at-time 1` and `--min-duration`, and nothing rejects the combination (line 144 only rejects the opposite direction).
